42862279.label: Objectives
42862279.text: To compare safety outcomes and toxicity patterns of glass and resin microspheres in patients undergoing yttrium-90 (⁹⁰Y) transarterial radioembolization (TARE) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), using uniform voxel-based dosimetry for both platforms and toxicity comparisons adjusted for treatment extent and tumor burden.

42862279.label: Materials and methods
42862279.text: This retrospective single-center study included 103 consecutive patients with HCC and preserved liver function treated with ⁹⁰Y-TARE between June 2020 and June 2024 using glass-based (n = 70) or resin-based (n = 33) microspheres, selected according to routine practice and product availability. Absorbed doses for both cohorts were derived from voxel-based ⁹⁹ᵐTc-MAA SPECT/CT dosimetry. Adverse events (AEs) were graded with CTCAE version 5.0. The primary endpoint was overall AE incidence; secondary endpoints were specific toxicity patterns and dose-toxicity associations, examined with multivariable logistic regression adjusting for treatment extent and tumor volume. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were compared with the log-rank test.

42862279.label: Results
42862279.text: Overall AE incidence did not differ between glass and resin microspheres (glass 37.1% vs. resin 30.3%; p = 0.497), and all AEs were grade 1-2. Tumor and non-tumorous liver absorbed doses were similar. Bilirubin toxicity was more frequent with glass microspheres (glass 28.6% vs. resin 9.1%; p = 0.027), whereas hemoglobin decline was more common with resin microspheres (glass 10.0% vs. resin 30.3%; p = 0.010); both exploratory differences persisted after adjustment for treatment extent and tumor volume. Lung shunt fraction, a baseline patient-level parameter, was higher with resin (glass 2.6% vs. resin 4.1%; p = 0.043). Higher lung absorbed dose was associated with AE occurrence overall, without a significant lung dose × microsphere-type interaction (p = 0.41). Neither PFS (median, glass 9 vs. resin 12 months; p = 0.868) nor OS (glass 23 vs. resin 29 months; p = 0.929) differed significantly.

42862279.label: Conclusions
42862279.text: Glass and resin microspheres showed no significant difference in overall AE incidence-without formally establishing equivalence-but differed in their patterns of mild laboratory toxicity independently of treatment extent and tumor burden. These exploratory findings support careful, individualized dosimetric assessment and require confirmation in prospective multicenter studies, but do not provide criteria for microsphere selection.

42912579.label: Purpose
42912579.text: This study was designed to investigate the detection rate and tumor uptake of 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET/CT in newly diagnosed high-risk prostate cancer (PCa), compared with 68 Ga-PSMA-11 and 18 F-FDG PET/CT.

42912579.label: Patients and methods
42912579.text: This study enrolled 48 patients with biopsy-diagnosed, treatment-naive high-risk PCa who underwent 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, 68 Ga-PSMA-11, and 18 F-FDG PET/CT between April and December 2024. A head-to-head comparison of detection rate and tumor uptake was performed among the 3 tracers. In addition, 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68 Ga-PSMA-11 dual-tracer PET was used to characterize the imaging phenotypes of each lesion and interlesional heterogeneity.

42912579.label: Results
42912579.text: A total of 477 lesions were detected by the 3 PET tracers. 68 Ga-PSMA-11 exhibited the highest overall detection rate (96.4%), followed by 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI (81.1%) and 18 F-FDG (66.0%). A total of 17 68 Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions were identified in 8 patients, all of which were detected by 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, whereas only 12 were detected by 18 F-FDG. Combined 68 Ga-PSMA-11 and 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET identified all lesions detected by triple-tracer PET. Based on relative tracer dominance of dual-tracer PET, patients were classified as PSMA-dominant (n=23), FAPI-dominant (n=5), or mixed phenotype (n=20). The mixed phenotype with marked interlesional heterogeneity might be associated with more advanced clinical characteristics, with a higher proportion of metastatic disease and a greater metastatic burden.

42912579.label: Conclusions
42912579.text: 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI is a promising PET tracer for newly diagnosed high-risk PCa. It may improve the detection rate of 68 Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions and provide complementary information that could reflect interlesional heterogeneity. The clinical value of combining 18 F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68 Ga-PSMA-11 PET requires further validation in larger prospective cohorts.

42957079.label: Objective
42957079.text: To evaluate longitudinal adoption of American College of Radiology (ACR) Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (TI-RADS) Terminology, report-level documentation of Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA) criteria, and associated ultrasound-guided FNA practice in a large multisite radiology network.

42957079.label: Methods
42957079.text: In this retrospective, multicenter study across 89 imaging sites, 304,455 diagnostic thyroid ultrasound reports (CPT 76536) and 11,246 ultrasound-guided FNA reports (CPT 10005/10006) from 2017 through 2023 were analyzed. A linked pre-biopsy cohort of 994 diagnostic reports immediately preceding FNA was examined. Automated text mining identified TI-RADS language and documentation of nodules meeting ACR size-based FNA thresholds. Trends were assessed using Cochran-Armitage, Spearman correlation, and χ2 tests.

42957079.label: Results
42957079.text: TI-RADS language increased from 1.6% of thyroid ultrasound reports in 2017 to 54.1% in 2023. Among 112,036 TI-RADS-containing reports, 11,845 (10.6%) documented nodules meeting FNA criteria. This proportion declined from 23.3% in 2017 to 8.0% in 2023, an absolute decline of 15.3 percentage points (Z = -47.94, P < 0.001) and was inversely correlated with annual TI-RADS adoption across the seven annual observations (ρ = -1.000, P < 0.001). Among FNA-indicated reports, TR4 predominated (56.9%), followed by TR3 (21.0%) and TR5 (19.4%); category distribution shifted significantly over time, although the effect size was small (χ2 = 169.91, P < 0.001; Cramér's V=0.086). In the pre-biopsy cohort (n=994), 498 (50.1%) contained TI-RADS language. The FNA rate per 1,000 thyroid ultrasound examination remained stable (29.1 in 2017; 27.7 in 2023).

42957079.label: Conclusion
42957079.text: ACR TI-RADS terminology use increased substantially but remained incomplete. Increasing terminology use was associated with declining report-level FNA eligibility. Biopsy appropriateness could not be assessed from report-level documentation alone.

42972079.text: Adrenal masses are found on roughly 4-5% of abdominal imaging studies, and the proportion rises with age. Most are benign, non-functioning adenomas that need imaging characterization and hormonal screening but no intervention. The remainder, comprising metastases, adrenocortical carcinoma, pheochromocytoma and hormonally active adenomas, raise questions that computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging cannot always settle; in these cases image-guided procedures can help. Percutaneous biopsy is reserved for hormonally inactive lesions whose benignity imaging has not established and whose histology would change management. Adrenal venous sampling remains the reference method for lateralizing aldosterone excess in primary aldosteronism and therefore decides who is offered adrenalectomy, although success depends heavily on operator experience and local protocol. Thermal ablation has produced biochemical and blood-pressure responses in selected aldosterone-producing adenomas and local control of limited metastases, but the evidence is largely nonrandomized and does not establish equivalence with surgery. Transarterial embolization serves three purposes: hemostasis in adrenal hemorrhage, devascularization before resection of hypervascular tumors, and functional treatment of aldosteronism, now supported by one small randomized trial. Each procedure carries hazards peculiar to the gland (catecholamine crisis, adrenal insufficiency after bilateral treatment, non-target embolization) that shape patient selection and periprocedural monitoring. This review covers indications, technique, outcomes and complications for each. Surgery remains the treatment of choice for most operable patients. Interventional radiology is most useful when the indications for sampling, ablation or embolization are recognized early and discussed at the multidisciplinary meeting, not only after surgery has been declined.

42980729.label: Objectives
42980729.text: To assess the feasibility of one-stop multi-energy dynamic volume perfusion photon-counting CT (VP-PCCT) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) evaluation, including lesion detection and correlations with histopathology.

42980729.label: Materials and methods
42980729.text: From July 2024 to June 2025, 407 participants with suspected malignant liver lesions prospectively underwent VP-PCCT, and 177 patients with pathology-confirmed HCC who received three-phase energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) were retrospectively enrolled for comparisons of image quality and lesion detectability. Single-phase images reconstructed from VP-PCCT perfusion datasets were compared with EID-CT. Perfusion parameters were analyzed between groups stratified separately by histological grade and microvascular invasion (MVI), and logistic regression was employed to identify independent indicators.

42980729.label: Results
42980729.text: Ninety-two participants [median age, 62 years (IQR, 53-69); 76 males] with pathology-confirmed HCC were included in the VP-PCCT group and matched with 92 in the EID-CT group. Compared with EID-CT, 40-keV VP-PCCT provided comparable image quality for HCC and vessels with a similar tumor detection rate but a lower radiation dose. Poorly-differentiated HCCs showed higher tumor hepatic perfusion index (HPItumor) and peritumoral blood flow (BFperitumor); MVI-positive HCCs exhibited lower tumor arterial liver perfusion (ALPtumor) and normalized blood flow of peritumoral region (BFnorm_peritumor) (all p < 0.05). HPItumor [odds ratio (OR): 1.06] and BFperitumor (OR: 1.04) were independent risk factors for poorly differentiated HCC, whereas decreased ALPtumor (OR: 0.97) and BFnorm_peritumor (OR: 0.25) were associated with MVI positivity (all p < 0.05).

42980729.label: Conclusions
42980729.text: One-stop VP-PCCT delivers high-quality morphologic and perfusion evaluation in a single low-dose scan, with hemodynamic profiles that may be associated with histological grade and MVI status.

42980729.label: Key points
42980729.text: Question Clinical use of dynamic volume perfusion CT for comprehensively evaluating HCC without additional multiphase contrast-enhanced imaging remains limited. Findings Multi-energy dynamic photon-counting perfusion CT provided high-quality morphologic imaging of HCC at a low dose, with perfusion parameters independently indicating poorly differentiated HCC and MVI. Critical relevance statement One-stop multi-energy dynamic photon-counting perfusion CT enables high-quality morphologic and functional assessment in a single low-dose scan, providing comprehensive HCC evaluation with hemodynamic profiling that may support the assessment of histological grade and MVI.

43002579.text: We report the 18F-Choline PET/CT findings of an intrathyroidal parathyroid adenoma (IPA) in a 30-year-old woman with primary hyperparathyroidism. Cervical ultrasound showed no parathyroid abnormality but revealed a hypoechoic nodule within the left thyroid lobe, initially misdiagnosed as a thyroid nodule. 18F-Choline PET/CT demonstrated intense focal uptake in the lesion, precisely localized to the intrathyroidal region. Postoperative pathology confirmed an IPA. This case highlights the value of 18F-Choline PET/CT in accurately localizing an IPA misdiagnosed as a thyroid nodule on ultrasound, thereby avoiding unnecessary fine-needle aspiration and thyroid surgery.

43019229.text: Primary amenorrhea is the absence of menarche in a 15-year-old adolescent girl who has developed secondary sex characteristics or a 13-year-old girl without development. Primary amenorrhea reflects disruption along the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian-uterine axis and may arise from a spectrum of anatomic, genetic, or functional abnormalities. Although primary amenorrhea is less common than secondary amenorrhea, recognition of the underlying level of dysfunction is essential for appropriate diagnosis and management as well as informed counseling regarding the patient's reproductive potential. A structured anatomic approach allows categorization of the causes into three levels based on the predominant site of dysfunction: level I, which involves the uterus and vaginal outflow tract; level II, which involves the ovaries and gonads; and level III, which involves the hypothalamus and pituitary gland. This classification system emphasizes a systematic and multidisciplinary approach to diagnosis and treatment, integrating clinical and biochemical testing and targeted imaging to localize the underlying dysfunction and guide treatment. Transabdominal US serves as the first-line imaging modality to help determine the presence and morphology of the pelvic organs. MRI provides detailed characterization of müllerian and urinary tract anomalies and allows evaluation of the hypothalamic-pituitary region when central causes are suspected.

43024029.text: Direct radiolabeling of cellular therapeutics and leukocytes represents a vital strategy for monitoring inflammatory loci and tracking cell-based therapies in vivo. While single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) agents, such as 111In-oxine and 99mTc-HMPAO, have long served as clinical mainstays, their utility is constrained by limited spatial resolution and suboptimal quantification. To address these limitations, we developed and preclinically validated 64Cu-labeled 2-methyl-8-hydroxyquinoline (64Cu-HMQ) as a neutral, lipophilic positron emission tomography (PET) tracer intended for high-resolution, quantitative cell-tracking paradigms (e.g., autologous leukocytes, stem cells, and immunotherapeutic vectors). 64Cu-HMQ was synthesized with high radiochemical yield (> 98%) and demonstrated robust in vitro stability in both formulation buffer and human serum over 12 h. The complex exhibited an optimal partition coefficient (logP = 1.4), providing the requisite membrane permeability for intracellular transport while maintaining adequate hydrophilicity. Baseline preclinical biodistribution and PET imaging in healthy rodents revealed favorable pharmacokinetic characteristics, marked by efficient blood and systemic clearance blood clearance, combined hepatobiliary and renal elimination, and minimal non-specific background accumulation. These foundational results establish the coordination integrity and intrinsic clearance kinetics of 64Cu-HMQ, demonstrating its strong translational potential as a long-lived (T1/2=12.7 h), quantitative PET alternative to conventional 111In-oxine for direct cell labeling and non-invasive PET cell tracking. In vitro leukocyte labeling confirmed high radiolabeling efficiency (71.2 ± 3.1%) with preserved cell viability (> 95%), highlighting its potential feasibility for cell-tracking applications.

43057879.text: The potential clinical benefit and impact on tolerability of combining androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 remain uncertain and were not evaluated in the primary analysis of VISION. In this secondary analysis, we assessed efficacy and safety of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 with and without concomitant ARPIs in previously treated patients (≥1 ARPI and 1 or 2 taxanes) with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (formerly metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer). Methods: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response, duration of PSA response, PSA progression-free survival (PSA-PFS), radiographic progression-free survival, overall survival (OS), and adverse events were explored in this post hoc analysis. For OS, a time-adjusted multivariate analysis was performed to control for biases. Results: Among patients randomized to [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617, 289 versus 262 in the full analysis set and 283 versus 246 patients in the safety analysis set received treatment with and without concomitant ARPIs, respectively. Among patients treated with versus without ARPIs, 49.7% versus 42.2% had a PSA response (≥50% reduction in PSA level) (odds ratio, 1.41; 95% CI, 0.93-2.13; nominal 2-sided P = 0.103), with a median response duration of 9.4 mo versus 8.8 mo, respectively. The median PSA-PFS was 8.6 mo versus 7.3 mo (hazard ratio, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.70-1.09; P = 0.120 [nominal 1-sided stratified log-rank test]). A time-adjusted multivariate analysis showed a median OS of 16.6 versus 13.3 mo (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.56-1.10; 2-sided P = 0.160). The frequency, nature, and severity of adverse events were similar between groups. Conclusion: The clinical benefits of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 were similar with and without concomitant ARPIs. The addition of concomitant ARPIs to [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 provided a numerically higher PSA response and a numerically greater median PSA-PFS and median OS.

43071179.label: Purpose
43071179.text: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic lung disease with variable clinical trajectories and treatment responses. CT depicts structural abnormalities but may not identify biologically abnormal lung. We evaluated pulmonary uptake of the hypoxia-sensitive tracer [¹⁸F]fluoromisonidazole ([¹⁸F]FMISO) in IPF and its cross-sectional associations with CT measurements and pulmonary function.

43071179.label: Methods
43071179.text: In this prospective proof-of-concept study with cross-sectional analyses, 10 participants with IPF and 10 age-matched healthy controls underwent [¹⁸F]FMISO PET/CT at 2 h and 4 h after injection. Whole-lung and CT-defined regional mean standardized uptake values (SUVmean) were measured. Post hoc sensitivity analyses were applied using CT-derived non-air-fraction correction to whole-lung SUVmean and to compartments below ​-400 HU and below ​-700 HU in both groups. Group comparisons accounted for independent and paired measurements. Pearson or Spearman coefficients correlations were used. Holm adjustment was applied within defined comparison families.

43071179.label: Results
43071179.text: Twenty male participants were included. At 4 h, uncorrected whole-lung SUVmean was higher in IPF than in healthy controls (0.521 ± 0.114 vs. 0.344 ± 0.050, adjusted p = 0.0028). After non-air-fraction correction, the difference persisted (mean difference: 0.158, pointwise 95% CI: 0.074-0.242, adjusted p = 0.0042). Corrected regional SUVmean at 4 h was also higher in IPF below -400 HU (1.721 ± 0.251 vs. 1.375 ± 0.220, adjusted p = 0.0215), with a consistent finding below ​-700 HU (adjusted p = 0.0054). Corrected mean comparisons at 2 h were non-significant with Welch's t tests. Within IPF, uncorrected whole-lung SUVmean at 4 h strongly correlated with mean lung attenuation (r = 0.812, adjusted p = 0.0172) and percent-predicted TLC (r = -0.794, adjusted p = 0.0244).

43071179.label: Conclusion
43071179.text: Higher [¹⁸F]FMISO uptake in IPF persisted at 4 h after estimated non-air-fraction correction in whole-lung and lower-attenuation regional measurements. Longitudinal validation of this potential imaging biomarker as a surrogate of hypoxia-specific trapping is required.
